composition.story: How does posting a journal entry change Cash? Start with an opening balance, then post an owner investment and a rent payment. Compare each highlighted Cash line with its ledger destination. Use Previous and Next to see which postings raise or lower the balance.

aha.observation: Posting preserves the journal side: Cash debits increase the balance, while Cash credits decrease it.

parts.presentation: Place below the story and instructions. Show the active state and completed trace on this rail, without timing or automatic advancement.

Use the approved fixed-picture arrangement with journal rows left and Cash ledger regions right. Keep positions unchanged. Highlight bound active regions and connecting links. Inactive destinations are guides, not posted entries; readout labels identify posting status. Keep monetary values exclusively in readouts.
Anchor the text beside its named target without covering labels. Present the reason as the bound status line beneath the picture.

Use four stable readout slots with wrapping labels. Values use whole USD, without rounding. Opening Cash is the reference balance. Current Cash equals opening Cash plus posted investment minus posted rent. Exclude unposted amounts from that calculation.

controls.presentation: Provide Previous and Next buttons. Default index is zero; bounds are zero through four, increment one. Retain button names when disabled at boundaries. variants.label: Fixed USD example: opening debit balance, owner investment, and rent payment. Cash is an asset; assume no other activity, fees, or taxes.

states.label: Opening Cash
states.sentence: Cash balance starts with an opening debit balance; both journal entries remain unposted.
states.why: The opening balance is the reference point for both postings.

states.label: Find investment Cash
states.sentence: Investment Cash is the journal debit to post into Cash.
states.why: Owner capital is the matching credit, but it belongs in a different ledger account.

states.label: Post the debit
states.sentence: Copy Investment Cash to Cash debit, preserving its amount and side.
states.why: Cash balance increases by the posted investment; the rent payment remains unposted.

states.label: Find rent Cash
states.sentence: Rent Cash is a credit, unlike the debit in Investment Cash.
states.why: Rent expense belongs in its own ledger; only the Cash line posts into Cash.

states.label: Post the credit
states.short: Both posted; debit adds, credit subtracts
states.sentence: Copy Rent Cash to Cash credit; this posting lowers Cash balance.
states.why: Both postings preserve their journal sides: the investment debit adds to Cash, while the rent credit subtracts.
